articles.title: Guided growth for idiopathic genu valgum: analyzing the incidence and risk of rebound.
articles.authors: Kohan Fortuna Figueira S, Turazza F, Halliburton C, Colombo C, Allende V, Puigdevall M, et al.
articles.population: Paediatric patients with idiopathic genu valgum treated with tension-band plates
articles.outcomes: Incidence of rebound after implant removal; factors associated with rebound risk; rate of surgical revision needed
articles.take_home: Two-thirds of children treated with guided growth plates for knock knees experienced some rebound (return of the knee angle) after the implants were removed, but few needed further surgery. Faster correction during treatment was linked to a higher chance of rebound.

articles.title: LongTerm Outcomes of Suspected Transient Synovitis of the Hip in NonAspirated Patients.
articles.authors: Smadi Z, Burnett J, Varghese J, Balaji S, Rosenfeld S
articles.population: Children with presumed transient synovitis of the hip managed without aspiration
articles.outcomes: Residual symptoms, recurrence of transient synovitis, rheumatologic or sequelae diagnoses, missed septic arthritis diagnosis at 4 weeks, 6 months, 1 year, 5 years and across mean 9.41 years follow-up
articles.take_home: Children with suspected transient synovitis treated without hip aspiration had very good long-term outcomes with no cases of missed septic arthritis, but 3.2% were later diagnosed with other conditions like juvenile arthritis, so continued follow-up is needed if symptoms are unusual, prolonged or return.

articles.title: Missing the Deadline: Predictors of Surgical Delay Beyond 18 Hours in Pediatric Supracondylar Humerus Fractures.
articles.authors: Johnson QJ, Varas-Rodriguez E, Sullivan MH, Wahlig BD, Broida SE, Stans A, et al.
articles.population: Children with supracondylar humerus fractures treated surgically
articles.outcomes: Time to operating room from emergency department presentation; predictors of surgical delay beyond 18 hours
articles.take_home: Only 16% of patients experienced delays beyond 18 hours, with average surgery time of 12.2 hours. Evening arrival at hospital and more severe fractures were associated with longer delays, likely due to system factors like transfers between hospitals rather than clinical outcome problems.

articles.title: Acute flexion contracture correction for failed distal femoral extension osteotomy in arthrogryposis: early results and complications.
articles.authors: Valles KF, Williams N, Nossov SB
articles.population: Children with arthrogryposis multiplex congenita who had failed distal femoral extension osteotomy
articles.outcomes: Correction of knee flexion contracture, arc of motion, ambulation status, and complications
articles.take_home: Posterior knee release with femoral shortening improved knee contractures and movement in children whose previous knee straightening surgery had failed. All children could walk after surgery, compared with only one-third before.

articles.title: Residual dynamic arch index but balanced plantar loading after medializing calcaneal osteotomy in children with symptomatic flexible flatfoot: a matched-pair pedobarographic study.
articles.authors: Ruampatana C, Osateerakun P, Chongpison Y, Seehaboot K, Limpaphayom N
articles.population: Children with symptomatic flexible flatfoot who had medializing calcaneal osteotomy, compared with healthy controls
articles.sample_size: 21 children with flatfoot matched to 21 controls (38 feet per group)
articles.outcomes: Dynamic arch index, regional plantar impulse, foot loading distribution, foot axis angle, stance phase timing
articles.take_home: After surgery, children's feet showed better balance in how pressure was distributed when walking, but the arch still remained flatter than normal and the foot was rotated outward. The forefoot push-off during walking was slightly shorter than in children without flatfoot.

articles.title: Risk factors for the severity of heterotopic ossification in children with cerebral palsy.
articles.authors: Oto O, Sarikaya IA, Gorgun B, Ertan Birsel S, Inan IH, Inan M
articles.population: Children with cerebral palsy who developed heterotopic ossification after hip reconstruction surgery
articles.outcomes: Severity of heterotopic ossification classified using a standardised classification system; association with demographic, clinical and surgical variables
articles.take_home: The study found no clear predictors of how severe heterotopic ossification becomes after hip surgery in children with cerebral palsy, although the results should be treated carefully because the study was relatively small.

articles.title: The public health challenges of children's and adolescents' digital media use: applying the digital determinants of health as an interpretive framework.
articles.authors: Holly L, Raeside R, Morton A, Shi J, Padmapriya N, Muller-Riemenschneider F
articles.outcomes: Mental, behavioural, physical, cognitive, and social health outcomes related to digital media use
articles.take_home: Digital media use in young people is associated with both benefits and harms, but more consistently linked to adverse health outcomes, with the effects varying by developmental stage. Current research focuses too much on simple measures like screen time and not enough on how platform design and commercial incentives shape young people's experiences.

articles.title: Governing the digital determinants of health for children and young people: a global public health imperative.
articles.authors: Prainsack B, Medhora RP, Kickbusch I
articles.outcomes: Governance frameworks for digital determinants of health across infrastructure, platform design, data governance, and institutional accountability
articles.take_home: This review argues that how digital systems are designed and governed significantly affects the health of children and young people, and that governments need coordinated public health policies to manage these digital systems rather than regulating individual technologies separately.

articles.title: Intravenous Dexamethasone Prolongs Opioid-Free Analgesia After Pediatric Hand Surgery: A Randomized Triple-Blind Trial.
articles.authors: Marszalek-Buko J, Reysner T, Perek A, Pietraszek P, Rosada-Kurasinska J, Batkowska-Sniatkowska A, et al.
articles.population: Children undergoing elective hand or wrist surgery
articles.outcomes: Time to first opioid use, opioid consumption, pain scores, time to finger movement, adverse events
articles.take_home: Adding dexamethasone to nerve blocks helped children stay without opioid painkillers for longer and needed fewer opioids overall after hand surgery, though it slightly delayed the return of finger movement. The higher the dexamethasone dose, the longer pain relief lasted without opioids.

articles.title: Outcomes of Surgical Interventions in Children With Fibrous Dysplasia/McCune-Albright Syndrome.
articles.authors: Bulaicon OO, van der Kruk J, Joustra S, van de Sande M, Appelman-Dijkstra NM, de Witte PB
articles.population: Children with fibrous dysplasia/McCune-Albright syndrome who had orthopaedic surgery before age 18
articles.outcomes: Risk of refracture or need for second surgery within 5 years; complications including refractures
articles.take_home: Most children with fibrous dysplasia/McCune-Albright syndrome needed surgery on the upper thighbone for fractures or impending fractures. Girls and children operated on at younger ages had higher chances of needing further surgery or experiencing another fracture within 5 years.

articles.title: Comparison of Changes in Gait Kinematics and Surgical Outcomes After Proximal and Distal Femoral Derotational Osteotomy in Children With Cerebral Palsy.
articles.authors: Hara R, Rethlefsen SA, Ponrartana A, Wren TAL, Kay RM
articles.population: Children with cerebral palsy undergoing femoral derotational osteotomy
articles.sample_size: 52 patients (91 limbs) with proximal osteotomy and 112 patients (177 limbs) with distal osteotomy
articles.outcomes: Hip rotation and foot progression angles during gait, complication rates, need for additional hardware removal surgery
articles.take_home: Both proximal and distal femoral osteotomies significantly improve hip rotation and foot progression in children with cerebral palsy. Proximal osteotomies required more additional surgery for hardware removal, whilst distal osteotomies had a slightly higher complication rate, so the choice of approach should consider these risks alongside other individual factors.

articles.title: Microstructural Vulnerability of the Tibial Tubercle Apophysis During Growth Hormone Therapy: A Multicenter Prospective Cohort Study Using Diffusion Tensor Imaging-MRI.
articles.authors: Fabricant PD, Beber SA, Perdomo-Luna C, Groff KD, Lu S, Kvist O, et al.
articles.population: Skeletally immature children and adolescents aged 6 years or older scheduled to start growth hormone therapy
articles.sample_size: 53 patients (68% male, 83% White, mean skeletal age 10 ± 3 years)
articles.outcomes: Changes in tibial tubercle physeal microstructure measured by diffusion tensor imaging-MRI, specifically apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), fractional anisotropy, and tract volume at baseline and 4, 8, and 12 months after growth hormone therapy initiation
articles.take_home: Growth hormone therapy causes temporary changes in the structure of the tibial tubercle growth plate, with the biggest changes at 8 months, which may explain why children on this treatment have an increased risk of tibial tubercle fractures. Doctors should consider limiting high-impact sports during the first year of growth hormone treatment.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted diagnosis of pediatric supracondylar humerus fractures: a deep learning-based clinical decision support model.
articles.authors: Gokceoglu YS, Darilmaz MF, Karadamar OL, Cig H
articles.sample_size: 1440 radiographs (720 fractures, 720 normal); 145 test set; 20 emergency physicians; 200 radiographs in reader study
articles.outcomes: Diagnostic accuracy, sensitivity and specificity for detecting supracondylar humerus fractures; comparison between artificial intelligence model and emergency physicians
articles.take_home: An artificial intelligence system performed similarly to emergency doctors at detecting supracondylar humerus fractures in children, but both missed some non-displaced fractures. The system could help with initial screening but cannot replace human doctors and needs further testing before use in clinical practice.

articles.title: Safe, Satisfied, and Home Early: Patient-Reported Outcomes of Next-Day Discharge Following Posterior Spinal Fusion for Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis.
articles.authors: Barre A, Kirk A, Prusick V, White S, Muchow R
articles.population: Adolescents aged 10 to 18 years with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis undergoing posterior spinal instrumented fusion
articles.sample_size: 91 patients with analysable data (32 next-day discharge, 59 postoperative day 2 or later)
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcomes including Scoliosis Research Society-22r scores, Spinal Appearance Questionnaire scores, and PROMIS domains at 6 months postoperatively
articles.take_home: Adolescents discharged the day after surgery for scoliosis fusion reported similar satisfaction and recovery outcomes as those staying longer in hospital, suggesting early discharge pathways can be safe and effective. Baseline patient measures did not predict which patients could safely be discharged early.

articles.title: Vitamin D Status, Supplementation and Radiographic Healing in Pediatric Both-Bone Forearm Fractures: A Prospective Controlled Study.
articles.authors: Balci EC, Karakas Balci D, Uslu M, Onaloglu Y, Sukuroglu A, Kucukberber S, et al.
articles.population: Children aged 5-12 years with both-bone forearm fractures treated conservatively, and healthy age-matched controls
articles.outcomes: Baseline vitamin D levels, prevalence of vitamin D deficiency, radiographic fracture union rates at 4, 6 and 12 weeks using modified Radiographic Union Score for Tibial fractures
articles.take_home: Children with lower vitamin D levels had slower fracture healing, and those given higher-dose vitamin D supplements (2000 IU daily) showed better healing rates than those given standard-dose (1000 IU daily). Correcting vitamin D deficiency early may help improve fracture healing in children.

articles.title: Reassessing the Kocher Criteria: A Prospective Evaluation of Diagnostic Performance in Pediatric Musculoskeletal Infection.
articles.authors: Rogie GA, Barksdale EM 3rd, Braithwaite HC 4th, Mo M, Clever D, Enata N, et al.
articles.population: Children aged 0 to 18 years presenting with suspected musculoskeletal infection
articles.sample_size: 102 patients (42 with transient synovitis, 30 with osteomyelitis, 30 with septic arthritis)
articles.outcomes: Diagnostic performance of the Kocher criteria and clinical variables in differentiating septic arthritis from transient synovitis and osteomyelitis
articles.take_home: The Kocher criteria are moderately helpful at distinguishing septic arthritis from transient synovitis, but cannot reliably tell the difference between septic arthritis and osteomyelitis because these conditions present very similarly. The study suggests the Kocher criteria should prompt further imaging tests like MRI rather than being used alone to decide on surgery.

articles.title: Radiologic Sequelae of Pediatric Septic Arthritis of the Shoulder: A Retrospective Series and Proposed Classification.
articles.authors: Agarwal A, Iqbal MZ, Khurana S, Gupta M, Sahoo S, Deep A
articles.population: Children treated for septic arthritis of the shoulder
articles.outcomes: Radiologic sequelae classified into 4 types: complete recovery (17.4%), epiphyseal irregularity/dysplasia (17.4%), physeal arrest/bar formation (47.8%), and articular destruction/proximal humeral loss (17.3%)
articles.take_home: Septic arthritis of the shoulder in children commonly causes permanent deformity on X-ray during follow-up, with most children developing growth plate injuries. Neonates and infants with additional bone infections elsewhere are at higher risk of severe long-term damage.

articles.title: Current concepts review: Low-vs high-tone neuromuscular spinal deformities: An evolving distinction with clinical implications.
articles.authors: Cetik RM, Studer D, Yazici M
articles.outcomes: Quality of life improvements, mortality reduction, preservation of pulmonary function
articles.take_home: Neuromuscular scoliosis is better classified by muscle tone (high-tone or low-tone) rather than nerve or muscle origin, as this helps doctors choose the right treatment approach. Surgery can safely improve quality of life and may help reduce deaths and preserve breathing function in these children.
